title: Delay (Time Lag)
equation: Perceived Effect = Actual Effect ÷ Time Delay
hook: Most people quit content right before it starts working, because month three looks exactly like month one.
statement: Cause and effect are often separated by a lot of time.
explainer: Content, referrals, relationships. The payoff shows up weeks or months later. Judge them by this week and you'll quit things that were actually working.
sop: Pick one system where results take a while, like content or referrals.
Estimate the realistic Time Delay in weeks.
Track whether you did the work, not whether results moved.
Set your review date at the end of that delay.
Don't quit before the delay has actually passed.
equation_example: Actual Effect 8, Time Delay 12 weeks. 8 ÷ 12 = 0.67. Lower means a long delay is hiding a real effect, so it feels like nothing's working when it is. Higher means you feel results almost right away.
question: Write down one thing you're close to quitting and how long it realistically needs.
closing_statement: Judge systems by their trajectory, not this week's result.
caption:
Principle Nº 116: Delay (Time Lag)

Most people quit content right before it starts working, because month three looks exactly like month one.

Cause and effect are often separated by a lot of time.

Your turn: Write down one thing you're close to quitting and how long it realistically needs.
